findings.reason: the plan names a branch its own cited code and cited run rule out, so the node hunts the wrong mechanism and the fixture cannot reproduce the reading, sending it into its own escape hatch and delivering nothing rather than the fix the observed row needs.
findings.text: §36's Why says "the only stream to read is the previous attempt's, so the run can read as gone and be drawn halted", pointing at `process_gone` → `_newest_stream_in_motion` → `_newest_stream_shows_work`; but `_newest_stream_shows_work` returns True whenever the newest stream holds any assistant record (`reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:1139-1182`), and the fixture calls for a predecessor that "delivered a complete manifest" whose `stream.jsonl` "ends with assistant and result records, as a finished worker's does" — the cited run's own `stream.jsonl` holds 140 assistant records, verified — while `_run_stream_quiet_seconds` caps the quiet at the current attempt's own clock (`min(quiet, launch)`, `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:641-649`), which §28 makes the 1 s-old new attempt, so `_run_stream_quiet_seconds` ≤ 1 s ≤ `LOG_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` (`reckon/crew/node.py:50`) and `_newest_stream_in_motion` is True whatever the predecessor stream's age; `process_gone` is therefore False (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:467-468`) and the fixture reads working, not halted

findings.reason: the symbol resolves one module away and a single grep recovers it, so it costs a reader a moment and misdirects no node's build.
findings.text: "`process_gone` goes through `_newest_stream_in_motion` to `_newest_stream_shows_work` in `reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py`" places the chain in `recovery_wait.py`, but `_newest_stream_in_motion` is defined in `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:194` and does not appear anywhere in `recovery_wait.py` (grep exits 1), so a reader resolving the named chain in the named file finds only its second hop

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass, with the citation imprecision recorded below — `STRANDED_LAUNCH_BOUND_SECONDS` (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:62`), `_attempt_started_seconds` (:436), `_resumed_launch_is_stranded` (:562), `_stranded_launch` (:581), `_run_stream_quiet_seconds` (:615) and `process_gone` (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:467`) all resolve; the cited run directory `r-20261016T013153737687-the-roadmap-lists-come-out-in-one-order` exists and its `attempt.json` records attempt 2 at `2026-10-16T02:09:29Z`; both test files §36 requires to pass unchanged (`tests/test_a_resumed_run_is_not_read_by_its_old_status.py`, `tests/test_a_delivered_run_waits_for_the_reflex.py`) exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §36's done-when names a buildable fixture, a measurable assertion (base reads halted, head does not, obligations raise no duty), a declared negative control (restore the named branch to its base behaviour), and a reproduce-first guard that stops the node rather than changing code if the reading cannot be reproduced.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is logged under the run directory and the gate logs sit on durable paths a later reader can open, not in a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §36's new names are mechanism words (`_resumed_launch_is_stranded`, "resume window", "attempt record"); no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, comment or filename, and no changelog prose is present.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §36 attributes the drawn `halted` row to `process_gone` reading the previous attempt's stream as gone, but the branch it names cannot fire for the very fixture the done-when specifies, because that stream holds assistant records and `_newest_stream_in_motion` therefore returns True.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: a run in the resume window whose new attempt has neither a stream nor a process record of its own reads starting/working, never halted.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §36 is `implementable`, its open followup `f-tmstwiw-036` (:453-457) carries the one-line invocation `/reckon-build the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches §36`, and every section it shares a write path with (`recovery_classification.py`: §33/§34/§35; `recovery_liveness.py`: §27/§28) is already `done`, so no ordering edge is outstanding against live work.
